facts.text: Traverse City earned the nickname “Cherry Capital of the World” because its surrounding Grand Traverse Bay area produces more cherries than any other U.S. region.
Founded in 1928, Interlochen Center for the Arts began as one of the nation’s first institutions dedicated to nurturing young artists.
Settled in 1847, Traverse City evolved from a timber town into a leading cherry‑processing hub and a year‑round resort destination.
Rail service reached Traverse City in December 1872 via a spur from the Grand Rapids and Indiana Railroad, sparking a tourist‑focused expansion two years later.
The Traverse City Film Festival ran annually from 2005 to 2019, showcasing independent cinema each July and August in the city’s historic venues.
